item.title: Instruction Tuning Sharpens Number-Choice Heuristics in Language Models
item.description:
Instruction Tuning Sharpens Number-Choice Heuristics in Language Models

🔎 Overview

“3, 7, 14, 17, 42: Instruction Tuning Installs and Sharpens Number-Choice Heuristics in Language Models” was submitted on 26 Oct 2026. The paper investigates how instruction‑tuned checkpoints change the way language models select integers when prompted for a random number.

🧪 Method

  • “We measure, without sampling error, the probability a language model assigns to each integer from 1 to N when asked for a random number.”
  • “For a fixed prompt the model defines one probability vector, which we compute by summing over each integer’s scored spellings rather than estimate by sampling, removing the noise that limits earlier studies.”
  • “We evaluate 18 open‑weight model lines at five ranges up to N = 100, under 29 decoding configurations, on two inference stacks; 15 of them have matched base and instruction‑tuned checkpoints that both give usable answers.”

⚙️ Key Findings

  • “Instruction tuning makes the distribution less uniform in all 15 pairs.”
  • “It installs one heuristic, round‑number avoidance, and sharpens another, endpoint avoidance.”
  • “Base checkpoints do not avoid round numbers once the endpoints are removed from those sets; tuned checkpoints avoid them, multiples of 10 almost completely.”
  • “Base checkpoints return the endpoints 1 and N at 0.30 to 0.60 of the interior rate; tuned checkpoints almost never return them.”
  • “A preference for odd numbers is consistent across tuned checkpoints only at N = 100, where base checkpoints also show it weakly.”
  • “Endpoint avoidance and the odd preference fit the account Kubovy and Psotka [6] proposed for human number choice; round‑number avoidance is not part of that account, and the midpoint avoidance it predicts is essentially absent, with one slight exception at N = 100.”
  • “Tuning does not install a new favourite integer shared across models: above N = 10 no modal integer is shared by more than 42 percent of tuned conditions, and P (17) rises in 10 of 15 pairs and falls in 5.”
  • “The concentration is present in the model’s own distribution: at temperature 1.0, nucleus truncation at top‑p 0.95 adds a median of 0.035 to the total variation distance.”

💡 Why It Matters

  • The results show that instruction tuning can embed human‑like number‑choice heuristics (endpoint and odd‑number biases) while also introducing a distinct round‑number avoidance pattern not seen in human studies.
  • Understanding these systematic biases is crucial for interpreting model outputs in applications that rely on random‑number generation or probabilistic sampling.
  • The work provides a noise‑free measurement approach that could be reused to study other latent preferences in language models.

Evidence drawn exclusively from the submitted manuscript (26 Oct 2026).

#instructiontuning #numberchoice #languagemodels

Source: 3, 7, 14, 17, 42: Instruction Tuning Installs and Sharpens Number-Choice Heuristics in Language Models Source: Causal Localization of Evidence Effects in Transformers Source: A Quantitative Approach to Asch Conformity in Frontier Large Language Models Source: Language Models Keep Abandoned Analyses: Residue and Adaptation after Garden-Path Sentences

item.title: Output Interface Shapes Evaluation of Instruction-Tuned Models
item.description:
Output Interface Shapes Evaluation of Instruction-Tuned Models

Researchers have shown that the surface format in which an answer is written – the output interface – can fundamentally confound how we judge both instruction‑tuning data quality and model performance.

🔍 Overview

  • Quality metrics for instruction‑tuning data and benchmark scores for tuned models both pass through an output interface.
  • The interface itself can hide or exaggerate a model’s true capability.

🧩 How it works

  • Gradient signatures were collected across 12 tasks, four semantically equivalent interfaces, three model families, and controlled corruptions.
  • The study demonstrated that the interface confounds both data‑quality and benchmark measurements.
  • Spectral statistics such as effective rank are mathematically invariant to rotating the interface and do not detect semantic corruptions.
  • The direction of the gradient update—not its magnitude—contains the signal about data quality.
  • The interface‑varying residual is informative: it perfectly identifies each unit’s target task across all three model families.

⚙️ Key details

  • Capability is stored relative to the training interface; a skill that adds >40 accuracy points in the training format can become almost invisible under other formats.
  • Adjusting a single generation budget can reverse the measured impact of fine‑tuning on the GSM8K benchmark, turning an apparent gain into a large loss.
  • Pre‑registered interventions define the limits where this geometric effect stops short of full control.
  • Both data quality and model capability are interface‑conditioned; current reporting practices often present the interface rather than the underlying content.

💡 Why it matters

  • Evaluations that ignore the role of the output interface risk mischaracterizing model abilities and the value of instruction‑tuning data.
  • Recognizing the interface’s influence can lead to more robust benchmarking and clearer interpretation of model improvements.

📊 Summary of findings

Aspect Observation
Interface effect on measurement Confounds quality metrics and benchmark scores
Spectral statistics (effective rank) Invariant to interface rotation; blind to semantic corruption
Update direction Carries quality signal
Interface‑varying residual Identifies each unit’s target task across families
Capability storage Relative to training interface; large gains can vanish under other formats
Generation budget correction Flips fine‑tuning effect on GSM8K from gain to large loss
Reporting practice Often presents interface instead of content

#AIEvaluation #InstructionTuning #ModelCapability #Benchmarking

Source: How Output Format Confounds Data Quality and Capability in Instruction Tuning
